mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 5% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly different from zero at 10% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 5% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average by more than 3% for four consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and signals negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA by > 3% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 10% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in GDPC1 and HOUST above their respective 3-month moving averages signals strengthening housing demand and economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 3-month MA and HOUST > 3-month MA simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly above zero at 5% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in FEDFUNDS and an increase in CPIAUCSL above 2.5% over two months signals a loss of monetary policy credibility, which erodes investor confidence and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS declines and CPIAUCSL > 2.5% for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 5% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent fall in PAYEMS below its 12-month moving average by more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates weakening employment, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenues, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 12-month MA by > 1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 10% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between rising RSAFS and higher S&P 500 forward returns over a 5-day horizon, as increased household savings can signal anticipated future consumption and corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: The correlation between RSAFS changes and S&P 500 5-day forward returns is not statistically significant at the 5% level in out-of-sample testing.
